definition: Large-scale Robust Visual, a large and diverse visual instruction tuning dataset.
details: Large-scale Robust Visual, a large and diverse visual instruction tuning dataset.

explainer.lead: LRV is a large, diverse dataset built for visual instruction tuning. Its scale and variety matter because instruction-tuned vision models generalise better when trained on broad rather than narrow data.

tiers.eli5: It's like a big, varied workbook full of picture-and-instruction pairs, so a model can practise following many different kinds of image requests.
tiers.practitioner: Used to fine-tune vision-language models to follow image instructions. A pitfall is assuming diversity guarantees coverage of your own domain's edge cases.
tiers.paperLevel: A visual instruction tuning dataset: image–instruction–response triples used for supervised fine-tuning; limits depend on its diversity relative to the target task.

explainer.example: A team fine-tunes a vision-language model on LRV so it can answer varied requests about images rather than only one narrow task.
